nodes.label: TrafficDemand OD Matrix Spec
nodes.rationale: Origin-destination travel demand specifications routing vehicle hourly volumes.

nodes.label: UrbanFlowGraph Schema Spec
nodes.rationale: Defines node/edge network structure, coordinates, lane capacities, speeds, and geographic projection.

nodes.label: OSMnx Road Ingestion & Consolidation
nodes.rationale: Extracts drivable OSM network and consolidates intersections within 15m to remove micro-junction artifacts.

nodes.label: IRC:106 Indian Urban Road Standards Imputation
nodes.norm_label: irc:106 indian urban road standards imputation
nodes.rationale: Fills missing lane, speed, and capacity tags using IRC:106 guidelines for primary, secondary, and tertiary roads in India.

nodes.label: One-Way Street Directionality Optimization
nodes.rationale: Converts bidirectional bottlenecks into high-capacity one-way corridors to maximize throughput.

nodes.label: InterventionPayload Schema Spec
nodes.rationale: Specifies road interventions: lane widening, one-way conversion, speed limit alteration, and road closures.

nodes.label: Intervention Evaluation Engine
nodes.rationale: Executes counterfactual simulation runs comparing baseline vs intervened network states.

nodes.label: Interactive Road Intervention Designer
nodes.rationale: UI controls allowing traffic engineers to click edges, toggle one-way direction, close streets, or widen lanes.

nodes.label: Corridor Alternative Analysis & Coupled Widening
nodes.rationale: Pairs high-congestion link closures with capacity widening on parallel corridors to avoid spillover bottlenecks.

nodes.label: Core Python Backend Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Specifications of backend packages including FastAPI, rustworkx, networkx, pydantic, and uvicorn.

nodes.label: UrbanFlow Optimization Platform
nodes.rationale: End-to-end urban mobility and traffic assignment platform combining graph theory, simulation, and intervention optimization.

nodes.label: Tarjan DFS Bridge-Finding Algorithm
nodes.rationale: Linear O(V+E) discovery of articulation points and bridges to protect road network connectivity.

nodes.label: Bottleneck and Bridge Cut-Edge Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Computes edge betweenness centrality and identifies cut-edges using Tarjan bridge detection to protect connectivity.

nodes.label: Bridge Filtering Safety Constraint
nodes.rationale: Guarantees the optimization engine will NEVER recommend closing a topological bridge (cut-edge) that would disconnect the graph.

nodes.label: Deck.gl Vector Map Visualization
nodes.rationale: GPU-accelerated WebGL line rendering visualizing traffic density, V/C ratios, and congested speeds.

nodes.label: UrbanFlow Frontend App Shell
nodes.rationale: HTML5 mount point, Inter/Outfit Google Font links, and viewport metadata for Deck.gl canvas.

nodes.label: Frontend PNPM Workspace
nodes.rationale: PNPM workspace definition configuring package boundaries.

nodes.label: UrbanFlow System Architecture
nodes.rationale: High-performance interactive traffic simulation and network optimization engine architecture separating simulation compute from web visualization.

nodes.label: Kochi Urban Road Network Scope
nodes.rationale: Defines geographic boundaries for Ernakulam CBD, Marine Drive, MG Road, and bypass corridors in Kochi, Kerala.

nodes.label: Rustworkx Multi-Origin Dijkstra Engine
nodes.rationale: High-performance Rust-backed graph library performing concurrent Dijkstra runs across batched origins.

nodes.label: SimulationResult Metric Schema
nodes.rationale: Standardized output schema providing link volumes, V/C ratios, congested speeds, and convergence stats.

nodes.label: BPR Congestion Performance Function
nodes.rationale: Standard Bureau of Public Roads polynomial volume-delay function with alpha and beta exponents.

nodes.label: Method of Successive Averages (MSA) Spec
nodes.rationale: Iterative equilibrium solver computing Wardrop user equilibrium using step size 1/k.

nodes.label: Mathematical Proof of Braess Paradox
nodes.rationale: Proves travel time increases from 65 to 80 minutes when a zero-cost shortcut is added due to selfish routing.

nodes.label: Wardrop User Equilibrium Principle
nodes.rationale: First Principle of User Equilibrium: journey times in all routes actually used are equal and less than those which would be experienced by a single vehicle on any unused route.

nodes.label: Braess Paradox Validation Suite
nodes.rationale: Synthetic validation network demonstrating that closing or adding a link can improve total system latency.
